newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian scientists seek nose to sniff out death.
newsitem.headline: Italian scientists seek nose to sniff out death.

text.p: Italian scientists believe that people who are dying give off a virtually indetectable odour and are trying to develop a special artificial nose to sniff out the "smell of death", La Repubblica reported on Thursday.
"The death odour is plausible and we are trying to find it," Giovanni Cristalli, a physiologist, told the newspaper.
"When a body dies, an emotional part lives on for a few seconds and at this moment, molecules with a particular odour are released," Cristalli added.
Scientists believe some animals, especially dogs and cats, may be able to smell the "death odour" but Cristalli said it was impossible for humans to detect it.
He said he was working with a team of scientists to develop an artificial device sensitive to the smell. "We are testing at least five artificial noses," he said.
Cristalli said the technique could even be used in future to detect whether a person has an undiagnosed cancer.
